eligibility_evidence.text: We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Sustainability Project Manager to lead the delivery of the Green Plan (2025-2028) across Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. The post holder will play a key role in driving forward carbon reduction initiatives, improving resource efficiency, and embedding sustainable practices across clinical and non-clinical services. The role requires strong project management skills, stakeholder engagement, and a solid understanding of sustainability within a healthcare setting. Applicants should have demonstrable experience delivering complex projects, ideally within the NHS or a similarly regulated environment, with a focus on environmental sustainability and organisational change. The successful applicant will join a collaborative and forward-thinking team, working closely with estates, procurement, clinical services, and corporate departments to deliver measurable environmental improvements. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a leading specialist NHS Trust, supporting innovation, education, and research while advancing sustainability across hospital and community settings. Moorfields is committed to delivering high-quality patient care alongside its environmental responsibilities, and this role will be instrumental in shaping and implementing sustainable healthcare practices across the organisation. To lead the delivery of sustainability projects across the Trust, ensuring alignment with the Moorfields Green Plan and wider NHS Net Zero targets. Toidentify, develop and implement initiatives that reduce carbon emissions, improve resource efficiency, and embed environmentally sustainable practices across clinical and non-clinical services. To support the development and monitoring of sustainability programmes, including data collection, analysis, and reporting on environmental performance. To ensure robust governance of projects, including risk management, financial oversight, and delivery against agreed timelines and outcomes. To provide expert advice and guidance on sustainability to colleagues across the organisation, promoting best practice and supporting behaviourchange initiatives. To contribute to staff engagement,education and training to embed a culture of sustainability throughout the Trust. To represent the Trust in regional and national sustainability networks, contributing to the development of NHS-wide initiatives and sharing learning and innovation. To support the Trust’s reputation as a leader in sustainable healthcare through collaboration, research, and continuous improvement. Join Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust At Moorfields, people’s sight matters - and so do the people who make it possible. For over 200 years, Moorfields has been at the forefront of ophthalmic care, research, and education. With more than 2,300 dedicated team members and over 700,000 patients seen annually across our City Road site and 22 networked sites, we are proud to be a global centre of excellence. We're also a vibrant community where kindness, equity and excellence shape every aspect of our work. Whether it’s pioneering research through our partnership with UCL Institute of Ophthalmology and Moorfields Biomedical Research Centre or training the next generation of global eye care leaders, we’re united by one mission - delivering world-class eye health, sustainably and at scale. And we’re just getting started. From 2027, we’ll move to our brand-new Oriel site in St Pancras, Camden - a state-of-the-art centre that will unite eye care, research, and education under one roof. This groundbreaking facility, developed in partnership with UCL Institute of Ophthalmology and Moorfields Eye Charity, will enable transformative innovation and collaboration like never before. Could you be part of this future? Make us more. PROJECT DELIVERY • Identify, initiate and co-ordinate appropriate project proposals to improve environmental sustainability.. • Ensure that project objectives, scope, deliverables, critical success factors and risks are clearly documented and agreed prior to project start. • Establish a project team with appropriate operational, clinical and corporate team membership. Co-ordinate the input of stakeholders and service users to ensure that appropriate options are appraised and delivered. • Perform benefits analysis and baseline current system performance before each project starts and ensure there is a plan in place for handover to the operational and clinical leads. • Preparation and maintenance of all project documentation, including (but not limited to): project brief, project initiation document, appraisal options, risks, issues, decisions, lessons learned and actions logs, high level and detailed project plans, highlight reports, Project Board reports and papers and contribution to Transformation Team Programme Board reports and papers. • Ensure all project documentation and reports are prepared and delivered as specified in the project communications plan and in line with agreed reporting schedules. • Set-up and lead project team meetings, involving stakeholders and project team members. Responsible for controlling, directing, planning and allocating work and motivating service users to get directly, or indirectly involved with the project and its development. • Manage the implementation costs and resourcesallocated to the project. • Co-ordinate the activity of project team members and contributors ensuring that tasks and work packages are completed satisfactorily and on schedule. • Regularly report on progress,monitoring progress against plan, delivery of the project objectives, and post project review including updating the lessons learned and decision logs. • Undertake anyadditionalduties appropriate to the post, as may be required by the service and as delegated by the Director for ServiceImprovement. COMMUNICATIONS • Provide advice and guidance to staff and managers across the Trust in relation to sustainability, act as an advocate and champion for sustainability. • Develop and maintain strong working relationships with a number of operational, clinical and corporate management teams including developing good knowledge of the overall programme aims, objectives and initiatives so as to provide meaningful expert advice. • Provide advice and guidance to staff and managers across the Trust in relation to sustainability. • Represent the Trust to contractors, suppliers and providers in furtherance of project objectives. • The post holder will be required to communicate and engage constructively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders on a range of highly complex, specialist and often contentious issues. FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY • Where relevant, responsibility for managing approved implementation costs and benefits delivery for projects, totalling a net worth between £50K to £2M. • To work within the Trust's standing financial instructions and controls. PEOPLE MANAGEMENT • Line management (as required) • Large scale (estimated 5-20 at any one time, manager and clinician level and above) relationship contacts requiring intensive influencing and relationship skills. • Role model the Moorfield’s Way values and behaviours both individually and through the team. • Ensure that behavioural expectations of team members are established. • Ensure responsible staff have clarity of role and appropriate training as required. • It is the post holder’s responsibility to ensure that they have undertaken all mandatory training, in line with Trust policies and procedures. Effective supervision of a project team where you do not have direct line management responsibility. Working with operational managers, frontline operational and clinical staff and third party contractors. Experience of business process mapping to identify and deliver change. Effective analytical and problem solving skills. Ability to analyse complex facts and situations and develop a range of options coupled with the ability to respond to sudden unexpected demands. Experience of report development and writing; ensuring the accuracy of information and effective translation for different audiences. Must have experience of managing internal and external stakeholder engagement, including managing relationships and coordinating work between cross-functional teams. Desirable criteria: Experience of operational and non-operational management in the NHS Knowledge Desirable criteria: • Working knowledge of a clinical operations environment and how to manage conflicting priorities to ensure projects are delivered. • Knowledge of current healthcare policy in the NHS and how this applies to the local health economy. Display integrity: • Encourage trust through own actions. • Enthusiastic self-starter with a positive committed and determined approach. • Professional and positive approach. • Be honest in dealing with others Desirable criteria • Understand the impact of own actions on the Trust and others in the Service Improvement team. WE ARE FELIX We bring people together to rescue, repurpose, and share surplus food that would otherwise go to waste, turning an environmental problem into a social opportunity. Together with 16 other independent charities, 18,000 volunteers, and thousands of partners, we are the UK’s food rescue network, supporting 1.5 million people across the country. We‘re about fuller plates, fuller communities, and fuller lives. PURPOSE OF THE JOB The Head of Comms and External Affairs will lead our narrative and steward our reputation at critical moment, following the merger of FareShare and The Felix Project to form the new Felix brand. The role will set the strategy and operating rhythm for a team of seven across media relations, internal communications and public affairs, ensuring Felix speaks with one clear, trusted and influential voice. Reporting to the Director of Marketing and Communications and working alongside the Head of Brand Marketing who leads brand marketing and digital communication, the postholder will protect and build Felix's reputation, shape national and sector conversations on food redistribution, food waste and food insecurity, and help position Felix as a leading partner in the national endeavour to triple food redistribution in the UK. The role will provide senior counsel to the CEO, Executive Team, trustees and senior leaders; lead high-quality media, stakeholder and parliamentary engagement; and ensure internal communications support colleagues, volunteers and partners through integration, change and growth. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES * Set and lead an integrated external affairs strategy for Felix, aligned to organisational strategy, the post-merger integration plan, the refreshed brand and the national programme to expand food redistribution. * Lead, develop and empower a multidisciplinary team of seven across media relations, internal communications and public affairs, directly managing three discipline leads and building clear priorities, standards and ways of working. * Lead Felix's media relations and reputation management, securing proactive national, regional and sector coverage, overseeing reactive press office activity, preparing spokespeople, managing issues and crisis communications and working closely with the digital marketing team. * Working closely with the CEO and policy colleagues, leading public affairs and influencing activity, building trusted relationships with government, parliament, food industry partners, redistribution networks, funders and sector coalitions to advance Felix's mission and policy objectives. * Set the strategic direction for internal communications, ensuring staff, volunteers, network partners and other internal audiences understand the charity's vision, values, priorities and change journey. * Develop clear narratives, messages, evidence and thought leadership that explain Felix's mission, impact and role in creating a fairer and more sustainable food system. * Provide expert advice to the Executive Director of Fundraising, Marketing and Communications, CEO, Executive Team, trustees and senior leaders on reputation, stakeholder positioning, media risk, political context and communications opportunities. * Work closely with the Head of Brand Marketing to ensure external affairs, brand marketing, fundraising, digital communication and operational communications are integrated, consistent and mutually reinforcing. * Embed professional standards, risk management, evaluation and compliance across the function, including political impartiality, charity law, safeguarding, data protection, media protocols and inclusive communications. * Bring innovation and experimentation to the development of content and wider communications offer. * Your normal duties and responsibilities will be set out in your job description. However, the charity may require you to perform other duties from time to time. PERSON SPECIFICATION * Strategic and mission-led: keeps the needs of communities, charity partners and the wider food system at the heart of decision-making. * Collaborative and integrative: works across disciplines and functions, building strong relationships with the Head of Brand Marketing and colleagues across fundraising, operations, network, policy and partnerships. * Empowering leader: sets clear expectations, coaches and develops others, creates psychological safety and builds a united, high-performing team. * Politically astute: reads the external environment well, exercises sound judgement and understands when to act, advise, pause or escalate. * Clear and compelling communicator simplifies complexity, crafts messages that cut through and adapts style for different audiences. * Agile and resilient: remains calm under pressure, handles ambiguity and supports teams through change and high-profile moments. * Evidence-led and impact-focused: uses data, insight and lived experience responsibly to make a stronger case for change. * Inclusive and values-driven: champions dignity, fairness, accessibility and representation in communications and leadership. * Accountable and delivery-focused: takes ownership of decisions, follows through on commitments and manages risk, budget and performance with discipline. ESSENTIAL CRITERIA * Significant senior experience in external affairs, communications, public affairs or strategic influencing, ideally in a charity, public policy, food, poverty, sustainability or highly scrutinised public-facing environment. * Track record of leading multidisciplinary communications or external affairs teams, including line management of managers and experience of building capability through change. * Strong media relations expertise, including national media, press office leadership, spokesperson preparation, issues management and crisis communications. * Deep understanding of UK public affairs and influencing, including working with parliament, government departments, civil servants, political advisers, local/regional leaders and sector coalitions. * Experience of internal communications during organisational change, merger, rebrand or transformation, with a strong understanding of how to build trust, clarity and engagement. * Excellent strategic judgement and ability to translate complex policy, operational and impact information into clear narratives that motivate audiences to act. * Proven ability to advise CEOs, executive teams, trustees and senior leaders with confidence, discretion and political sensitivity. * Strong stakeholder relationship skills, including the ability to convene partners across food industry, voluntary sector, government, philanthropy, community organisations and internal teams. * Experience of planning, budgeting, commissioning agencies or suppliers, and evaluating communications and influencing impact using qualitative and quantitative measures. * Knowledge of charity governance, political neutrality, safeguarding, data protection, brand/reputation risk and inclusive communications standards. * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including speeches, briefings, media lines, policy positions, internal updates and board-level papers. * Personal commitment to Felix's mission to rescue good food and get it to people and places that need it, and to equity, diversity, inclusion and the dignity of people experiencing food insecurity. EQUITY DIVERSITY INCLUSION & BELONGING At Felix, we are committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion in everything we do. We value the unique contributions of every individual and strive to create a respectful, inclusive environment free from discrimination or prejudice. Our commitment extends to all employees, and volunteers, ensuring equal opportunities for everyone, regardless of background or characteristics. APPLICATION PROCEDURE Once you apply you will be directed to our recruitment portal. Please upload your CV and a covering letter outlining your suitability for the role and make sure that they are both uploaded before submitting your application. After you have submitted your application, you have 24 hours in which you can access you application and make edits. We will only consider applications with both CV and cover letter submitted. RECRUITMENT TIMELINE We reserve the right to close advertisements early and we might assess candidates and arranging interview as applications come in, so please apply as soon as possible, to avoid missing out on this opportunity. Due to the anticipated large number of applicants, if you do not hear from us within four weeks of your application, we regret to inform you that your application has been unsuccessful. eligibility_evidence.text: We are seeking an exceptional leader to join our executive team asDirector of Corporate Affairs (Trust Secretary). Reporting directly to the Chief Executive, this pivotal role will make a significant contribution to the governance, strategic direction and long-term success of the Trust. As a trusted adviser to the Chief Executive, Board of Directors and Council of Members, you will lead the Corporate Affairs function, oversee governance arrangements and ensure the highest standards of corporate governance, decision-making and regulatory compliance. This is an exciting time to join the organisation as we prepare to move toOriel. Oriel will bring together clinicians, researchers, educators and industry partners in a world-class environment, transforming the way eye care is delivered and developed for future generations. As our new Director of Corporate Affairs, you will play a key role in supporting the Board to deliver strategic priorities, drive organisational improvement and ensure the Trust remains well-led, innovative and focused on outstanding outcomes for patients. You will help shape the future of one of the world's leading ophthalmic organisations while leading high-profile programmes, strengthening governance and building strong partnerships across the Trust, the NHS and wider health system. This is a unique opportunity for an experienced governance professional and strategic leader who thrives in complex environments and can influence at the highest level. As our new Director of Corporate Affairs, you will: • Be a trusted adviser to the Board, Chief Executive and Council of Members, ensuring the highest standards of corporate governance and decision-making. • Provide strategic leadership across Corporate Affairs, the Trust Secretariat and Information Governance functions. • Lead the governance processes that support the Trust Board, Executive Committee and Council of Members, enabling effective oversight and organisational performance. • Work alongside the Chief Executive and Executive Team to deliver strategic priorities, major transformation programmes and organisational objectives. • Drive continuous improvement in governance, risk management and Board effectiveness, helping to ensure the organisation remains well-led. • Build strong relationships with regulators, system partners and senior stakeholders, acting as an influential ambassador for the Trust. • Oversee the production of key statutory and corporate documents, including the Annual Report, ensuring compliance and transparency. • Lead and develop high-performing teams while ensuring the effective stewardship of corporate resources and budgets. This role offers the opportunity to work at the heart of the organisation, partnering closely with the Chief Executive, Executive Team, Board members, clinical leaders and external stakeholders across the NHS. You will play a critical role in ensuring the organisation is well-led, strategically focused and equipped to meet future opportunities and challenges. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected and able to contribute to their fullest potential. For a detailed job description and person specification, please download the attached. eligibility_evidence.text: Your new company We are currently partnered with a leading global biopharmaceutical organisation to recruit a Science Communications Senior Manager on an initial 12-month contract. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced communications professional to play a key role in shaping and delivering high-impact science communications across R&D, Medical and Corporate Affairs audiences.The successful candidate will help bring the organisation's science narrative to life internally, ensuring colleagues are informed, engaged and connected to key pipeline, medical and R&D milestones. Working closely with senior stakeholders across Global R&D, Medical and Corporate Affairs, you will develop compelling content, manage internal channels and support strategic communications activity across a complex, global environment. Your new role Develop and deliver internal science communications campaigns focused on employee engagement across R&D, Medical and pipeline activity. Create engaging stories, articles and content that communicate scientific progress, key assets and people-focused achievements. Own and maintain internal science communications channels and content calendars, including pages covering Medical, R&D and broader science-related updates. Lead the planning and delivery of R&D and Medical town halls, including agenda development, slide creation, speaker briefing and event coordination. Support internal and selected external awareness campaigns around key milestones, disease awareness days and corporate science initiatives. Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure messaging is accurate, consistent and aligned across internal and external platforms. Develop materials and resources that communicate R&D, medical programmes and partnering activity clearly and effectively. What you'll need to succeed Strong experience developing and executing strategic communications programmes for internal and external audiences. Proven background in scientific, medical, pharmaceutical, R&D, brand or franchise communications. Excellent internal communications, employee engagement and event delivery experience. Confident producing high-quality written materials for a range of audiences, including healthcare professionals, scientists, biotech stakeholders, patients and the public. Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders. Experience in oncology, rare disease or neuroscience would be highly advantageous. Leadership communications experience and in-house pharmaceutical or biotech experience would be beneficial. Degree-level education is required; a scientific background is preferred. Fluent English is essential; French language skills would be advantageous. What you need to do now This is a fantastic opportunity to join a global, science-led organisation in a highly visible communications role, working at the intersection of R&D, Medical and Corporate Affairs. You will have the chance to shape engaging content, influence internal understanding of scientific progress and contribute to meaningful communications activity across a global business. Before you apply for this position, it is vital that you are in possession of an EU or UK passport or relevant visa to work without restrictions in the UK. If you are an experienced science, medical or internal communications professional available for a 12-month contract, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call Roberta Atkins on 0203 465 0045. Hybrid Contract Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Clinical Responsibilities Undertake comprehensive mental health, psychosocial, and risk assessments for service users experiencing homelessness. Assess, monitor, and manage risks relating to self-harm, suicide, exploitation, self-neglect, substance misuse, safeguarding, and risks to others. Develop, implement, and regularly review recovery-focused, person-centred care plans. Provide evidence-based mental health interventions and therapeutic support. Monitor mental and physical health needs and facilitate access to primary and secondary healthcare services. Administer and monitor prescribed medication, including depot injections where required. Identify deterioration in mental state and coordinate timely interventions to prevent relapse and unnecessary hospital admissions. Care Coordination and Case Management Manage a caseload of service users with severe and enduring mental illness and complex social needs. Act as Care Coordinator in accordance with the Care Programme Approach (CPA) and Trust policies. Support service users to engage with mental health services, housing providers, benefits systems, and community resources. Promote service user involvement in care planning, goal setting, and decision-making. Facilitate discharge planning and continuity of care following inpatient admissions. Homelessness and Housing Support Work closely with Westminster City Council, outreach teams, housing providers, hostels, and supported accommodation services. Contribute to housing assessments and support pathways into appropriate accommodation. Assist service users in maintaining tenancy arrangements and reducing the risk of repeat homelessness. Support individuals who have difficulty engaging with statutory services through assertive outreach and flexible engagement approaches. Multi-Agency Working Work collaboratively with psychiatrists, GPs, social workers, occupational therapists, substance misuse services, probation services, safeguarding teams, and voluntary organisations. Participate in multidisciplinary meetings and case conferences. Provide specialist mental health advice and consultation to partner agencies working with homeless individuals. Advocate for service users to ensure equitable access to healthcare, housing, and social care provisions. Safeguarding and Risk management Identify and respond appropriately to adult and child safeguarding concerns. Lead on risk management planning and ensure appropriate safeguarding procedures are followed. Contribute to Mental Health Act assessments and Mental Capacity Act processes as required. Maintain professional accountability for decision-making in complex and high-risk situations. Professional and Leadership Responsibilities Provide supervision, support, and mentorship to junior staff, students, and support workers. Contribute to service development, clinical audits, and quality improvement initiatives. Maintain accurate, timely, and legally compliant clinical records. Uphold NMC standards, Trust policies, and evidence-based practice. Participate in continuing professional development and mandatory training. Assertive Outreach and Engagement Conduct assessments and interventions in a range of community settings including streets, hostels, temporary accommodation, day centres, supported housing, and healthcare settings. Use assertive outreach approaches to engage individuals who are reluctant or unable to access mainstream mental health services. Develop therapeutic relationships with individuals who may have experienced trauma, exclusion, and repeated disengagement from services. Work flexibly to improve engagement and continuity of care. Maintain professional boundaries while building trust with vulnerable individuals.. Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Young Elite Management is a sports management mentoring company, registered as a Community Interest Company, that will offer sports management and mentoring services (initially football but longer term the plan is to extend to other sports). These services will include identifying young talented players from communities and areas, offering opportunities to train through recommended coaching services, and also ensuring they are given effective mentoring and guidance to remain focused. The overall company slogan and aim being ‘combining talent with guidance and opportunity’ as well as ‘Providing effective mentoring for sport enhancement’. The Duties We are recruiting for a professional Community Sports Coach Coordinator to maintain all community outreach activities. You will be required to represent the company and work with the management team to develop and implement initiatives that increase company visibility within the surrounding community. As a sports coach, you may provide nutrition and diet plans for athletes in addition to training plans. You may provide advice on a healthy lifestyle, including what to eat, getting enough sleep and relaxation techniques. Working with professional athletes may involve performance-enhancing and personal development advice. You inspire athletes to strive for their best performance and to develop their knowledge and techniques. You explain sports psychology and sports science to inspire confidence and a belief in their abilities as an athlete. Also, you may liaise with physiotherapists and nutritionists to provide and get additional support. A sports coach's role and skills can vary depending on where you work. Sports coaches work with individuals and teams at professional and amateur clubs, community sports associations, schools, colleges and universities. They may plan a recruitment drive to find new players and organise sporting events. As a sports coach, your primary roles may include: • Evaluate performance and provide suitable feedback, balancing criticism with positivity and motivation • Assess strengths and weaknesses in a participant's performance and identify areas for further development • Adapt to the needs and interests of group or individual participants • Communicate instructions and commands using clear communication methods • Demonstrate an activity by breaking the task down into a sequence • Encourage participants to gain and develop skills, knowledge and techniques • Ensure that participants train and perform to a high standard of health and safety at all times • Inspire confidence and self-belief • develop knowledge and understanding of fitness, injury, sports psychology, nutrition and sports science • Conducting Outreach methods to work with athletes within the community • Advising Athletes • Suggesting New techniques • Being a role model • Offering lifestyle advice • Organising competitions and meetings. On-site Temporary Part time

eligibility_evidence.text: We are looking for an Assistant Psychologist to join our friendly and specialist Adult Autism Service, supporting autistic adults (without a learning disability) across Westminster, Kensington and Chelsea, and Hammersmith & Fulham. Our service provides autism diagnostic assessments, post-diagnostic support, and consultation for adults and the people who support them. We work in partnership with local health, social care, and voluntary sector organisations to deliver person-centred, neuroaffirmative care. This fixed-term opportunity runs until 31 March 2027, with the potential for extension. Please respond to the additional application questions in your own words, drawing on your knowledge, experiences and reflections. As an Assistant Psychologist, you will support the delivery of high-quality, neuroaffirmative care within our specialist adult autism service. Working closely with experienced Clinical Psychologists and the wider multidisciplinary team, you will receive regular supervision and opportunities to develop your skills. We are looking for someone who can demonstrate: • A compassionate, person-centred and neuroaffirmative approach. • The ability to manage a varied workload and prioritise tasks effectively, with appropriate supervision. • A collaborative approach to working with colleagues across health, social care and partner organisations. • Knowledge of, or an interest in, services supporting autistic adults. • Strong communication, organisational and IT skills relevant to the role. • A BPS-accredited first-class or upper second-class (2:1) undergraduate degree in Psychology,or a Master's degree in Psychology, providing eligibility for Graduate Basis for Chartered Membership (GBC) of the British Psychological Society. Our service has strong links with North London Clinical Psychology Doctoral Training programmes and regularly supports trainee clinical psychologists through clinical placements, providing an excellent environment for learning and professional development. We are proud to be one of the largest community healthcare providers in the country, with more than 4,500 colleagues caring for over four million people across London and Hertfordshire. Every day, our teams bring their skill, compassion, and determination to the people who depend on us. What inspires us is at the heart of who we are: when we work together, we can help people move forward in ways that truly matter. Our teams support children as they take their first steps in life, and they stand beside adults as they rebuild strength, confidence, and independence. From newborn health visiting to community nursing, stroke rehabilitation, and palliative care, we are there for people through some of life’s most important moments. Joining Central London Community Healthcare means becoming part of a community that lifts each other up. It means working in an organisation that values compassion, welcomes new ideas, and believes in the potential of every colleague. Your development matters here. Your wellbeing matters. Your voice helps shape the future of the care we provide. We offer a competitive employment package because the work you do matters. At Central London Community Healthcare, you will join an inclusive organisation that invests in its people, supports development, and helps you thrive while delivering high-quality care. Applicants are expected to present clear and relevant evidence of the competencies and responsibilities detailed in the attached Job Description and Person Specification, together with a demonstrated commitment to the Trust’s values of Accountability, Inclusion, Compassion, and Empowerment. Are you looking to develop your career in psychology while making a meaningful difference to the lives of adults with learning disabilities? We are seeking an Assistant Psychologist to join our well-established Tri-borough Learning Disabilities Service in Kensington and Chelsea. Our multidisciplinary team works closely with the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea Learning Disabilities Social Care Team to deliver high-quality, person-centred care. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your clinical skills while supporting adults with learning disabilities, autism and people whose behaviour may be perceived as challenging. You will work directly with service users, families, carers and partner organisations, while receiving regular supervision from experienced psychologists. You will hold a degree in Psychology (or postgraduate qualification in Psychology) and have knowledge of research methods, data analysis and IT systems, alongside the ability to communicate information clearly and accurately in writing. An understanding of learning disability services and the ability to work collaboratively are important. Relevant experience may have been gained through employment, placements, voluntary work or other settings. eligibility_evidence.text: A Vacancy at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. An excellent opportunity has arisen for physiotherapists with an interest in neurorehabilitation and community working to join the Lambeth and Southwark Community Stroke and Neuro Rehabilitation Service (CSNRS). The service is recruiting to x3 Specialist Physiotherapy posts. We will be offering x2 posts which are permanent 12-monthly rotations between the Community Stroke Team and the Community Neuro Rehab Team. The 3rd post is a 12-month fixed-term contract with the Community Neuro Rehab Team. Our service aims to provide client-centred, evidence based multidisciplinary community neurorehabilitation to adults in the London Boroughs of Lambeth and Southwark. There are five teams within the CSNRS including: • Community Stroke Team • Community Neuro Rehab Team • 2b Neurorehabilitation Beds (Pulross Centre) • Southeast London Neuro Navigation Service • Community Spasticity Service You will be expected to provide a high standard of physiotherapy, undertaking all aspects of physiotherapist duties as an autonomous practitioner. Regular supervision and support is provided and there is a robust programme of in-service training to assist your development as a Specialist Physiotherapist. Please note, due to the high volume of applications expected, this advert may close earlier than the stated closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as soon as possible. This is a rotational Band 6 Specialist Physiotherapist post within the Community Stroke and Neuro Rehabilitation Service. The post holder will rotate between the Community Stroke Team and the Community Neuro Rehabilitation Team. We are also offering a 12-month fixed term contract in the Community Neuro Rehab Team. The post holder will provide specialist client-focussed Physiotherapy to individuals as part of the multidisciplinary team and will work closely with other members of the team to ensure a coordinated approach to client care. The post holder will independently and effectively manage a caseload of individuals with a neurological diagnosis. The post holder will provide specialist Physiotherapy assessment and treatment for adults in their own homes and other community settings. They will use evidence based, client-centred principles and a self-management approach to: • Assess, plan, implement and evaluate interventions. • Encourage patients to participate actively in their rehabilitation. • Maximise independence and support quality of life. The post holder will be expected to achieve agreed individual activity targets (face-to-face and/or virtual contacts) and be flexible in supporting wider caseload management. The post holder will be expected to supervise junior staff, incl. Clinical Assistants and Physiotherapy Students as required. They will participate in regular supervision, annual appraisal and continuing professional development. Guy’s and St Thomas’ is among the UK’s busiest and most successful NHS foundation trusts. We provide a full range of hospital and community services for people in south London and as well as specialist care for patients from further afield including cancer, renal, orthopaedic, respiratory and cardiovascular services. Our adult community services teams deliver care at the heart of the local communities we serve, working in partnership with GPs, local authorities and other healthcare and voluntary sector organisations. Working with our partners in Lambeth and Southwark, we are focusing on new ways of working to improve care for local patients. We have a reputation for clinical excellence and high quality teaching and research. We are part of King’s Health Partners, one of eight accredited UK academic health sciences centres. The commitment of our 23,500 staff is key to our success. We are one of the largest local employers and we aim to develop and support all our staff so they are able to deliver high quality, safe and efficient care. The 2019 NHS staff survey results show that we have one of the most engaged and motivated workforces in the NHS. We know this has a positive impact on the care provided to our patients. It is important that we all understand and reflect the trust values in our work. We are: Caring – we put patients first Ambitious – we innovate and strive for excellence Inclusive – we respect each other and work collaboratively Professional The post holder will: • Work as an autonomous practitioner within the standards of professional practice outlined by the Chartered Society of Physiotherapists (CSP) and Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). Be professionally and legally accountable for all aspects of own work. • Maintain close liaison with other senior colleagues in the team and ensure effective communication with all team members for day-to-day running of the service. • Keep updated of current issues with the profession, taking responsibility for personal growth and development such as reading relevant journal and research papers, participating in training opportunities and support research / quality improvement projects. • Maintain and record ongoing continuing professional development, using a professional portfolio. • Attend professional body / clinical interest group meetings as appropriate. • Participate in the delivery of training for physiotherapy students and fulfil clinical educator role. • Contribute to multidisciplinary and uni-disciplinary in-service training programmes. • Actively contribute to and be supported in developing knowledge and skills outlined in Personal Development Plans, sharing learning with colleagues. Clinical The post holder will: • Undertake specialist assessments of clients with a wide range of physical, cognitive and communicative impairments arising from neurological conditions with multiple co-morbidities and complex needs, including end of life conditions. • Provide comprehensive assessment, treatment and management to a caseload of adult patients with a wide range of neurological conditions following local operational policies and agreed standards and guidelines. • Analyse and provide specialist interventions based on clinical reasoning and evidence based practice to address therapeutic goals and optimise independence. • Monitor the effectiveness of interventions through goal setting, outcome measurement and evaluation of practice. • Be responsible for prioritising, delegating and managing own caseload and workload, including achieving agreed activity targets. • Work collaboratively with individuals, clients, families and carers, members of the multidisciplinary team and external agencies to ensure a coordinated approach to service delivery. • Discuss, advise and plan appropriate goals with clients, carers and the multidisciplinary team. • Effectively communicate with all appropriate people and organisations to provide and receive all relevant information pertaining to each client. This includes clients with complex emotional, physical, cognitive and communication impairments. • Use a self-management approach to empower individuals to take responsibility for their rehabilitation. • Respect clients’ dignity, privacy, culture and wishes during treatment, with a commitment to equitable access to rehabilitation. • Maintain and develop close links with colleagues in the acute sector, local authority, voluntary organisations and other members of primary healthcare services. • Be accountable for own professional practice and the support staff and students you are responsible for. • To work autonomously, ensuring personal responsibility for following lone working policies and procedures when accessing the community and client’s place of residence. • Attend multidisciplinary team meetings, case conferences, family meetings and other professional meetings as required. • Participate in the Trust staff appraisal scheme and supervision structure. • Be responsible for adhering to infection prevention and control policies within community settings. • Be responsible for safekeeping, cleanliness and maintenance of equipment, ensuring standards of infection prevention and control are met, including reporting on RADAR all incidents, accidents and complaints to the supervisor and/or manager. • Participate in ongoing review of service delivery and any developments in the service. Information Management The post holder will: • Keep accurate and contemporaneous records of assessment and treatment in accordance with standards set and input data on to the electronic records system (Epic). • Provide accurate and timely statistical data, i.e. SSNAP. Education and Professional Development The post holder will: • Contribute to the planning, organisation and delivery of training for staff in the service and from other disciplines and organisations through in-service training, supervision, joint working and practical demonstrations. • Contribute to student clinical education and development. • Assist with service development and service promotion. • Undertake all mandatory and statutory training in line with Trust policy. • Maintain and record ongoing professional development through formal peer review and use of a professional portfolio. This advert closes on Wednesday 12 Aug 2026. Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: A Vacancy at Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust. Are you passionate about helping others live meaningful lives? Join CNWL as a Band 6 Senior Community Occupational Therapist at the St John’s Wood Community Mental Health Hub, where we promote a supportive, inclusive and reflective workplace. As part of a multidisciplinary team, you will deliver recovery-focused, person-centred care to adults with a range of mental health needs. You will manage a caseload, providing occupational therapy assessments, interventions and psychosocial support, while working closely with service users, carers and partner agencies to promote recovery, reduce risk and support independent living. We are committed to staff wellbeing and professional development, offering flexible working, regular supervision and protected time for reflection and learning. Occupational Therapists have access to role-specific training, including psychosocial interventions, leadership development opportunities and pathways to broaden or specialise their practice in community mental health. This is an excellent opportunity to work in a forward-thinking service that values clinical autonomy, multidisciplinary collaboration and high-quality care. You will play a key role in supporting people on their recovery journey while developing your own skills and career within a supportive organisation. The service operates Monday to Friday, from 9:00am to 5:00pm. Job Summary As a Band 6 Senior Community Occupational Therapist, you will provide specialist occupational therapy assessment, intervention and advice within a multidisciplinary community mental health team. Using evidence-based and recovery-focused practice, you will support individuals to improve their occupational performance, independence, wellbeing and self-management skills. You will manage a caseload of service users with identified occupational needs, delivering both individual and group interventions, conducting functional assessments and developing person-centred care plans. You will work collaboratively with service users, carers, partner agencies and community organisations to promote recovery and support people to achieve their goals. The role requires a strong understanding of the impact of mental and physical health conditions on daily functioning, including providing advice on lifestyle adaptations, environmental modifications and equipment where appropriate. You will contribute to the wider function of the team, including duty responsibilities, and play an active role in service development. In addition, you will support the learning and development of others through supervision of junior staff, appraisal processes and practice educator for occupational therapy students on placement. You will integrate evidence-based practice with recovery principles to deliver high-quality, person-centred care that enhances quality of life and community participation. Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust offers its staff ongoing career progression through: · Monthly supervision · Annual personal development plans/appraisals · Access to exciting internal and external training opportunities. · In House OT to OT Training Excellent progression through various career pathway opportunities such as but not limited to: · Preceptorship Programme · Band 6 Development Programme · Hidden Gem and Annual Award Ceremonies Excellent staff benefits, our benefit packages are amongst the best in London and include: · Health and wellbeing services · Season ticket loans · Cycle to work scheme The trust also values its staff and you are entitled to become a member of MyTrustBenefits. MyTrustBenefits is an online portal for all CNWL staff, as well as their family and friends. It offers over 1400 discounts at hundreds of retailers nationwide. Save money on your weekly food shops, toiletries, cosmetics, cinema, meals out, holidays, travel and entertainment. You can also access free online courses on a variety of topics, professional and personal, ranging from business management, languages, law and teaching. Please see attached JD&PS for full details of duties and responsibilities Clinical • To manage a caseload of service users with multiple, enduring and complex mental health needs through provision of therapeutic care and treatment in the individual’s own home and other community venues. • To provide specialist, culturally appropriate, evidence based occupational therapy assessments for service users within the hub in order to establish and meet their occupational needs. • To provide full vocational needs assessment, advice and on-going intervention related to an individual’s vocational needs. • To select and use validated standardised assessment tools routinely and in practice, exhibiting clinical reasoning skills; to include the Model of Human Occupation (MOHO) assessments. • To apply specialist clinical knowledge and skills to carry out evidence based occupational therapy interventions, both individual and in groups, which are underpinned by relevant theoretical approaches and in line with the Trust’s Research and Development Strategy. • To lead and supervise junior staff in this practice as required. • To plan, implement and review individually tailored program of intervention using individual and group work approaches. • To develop, implement and review care plans using DIALOG + as a framework to complete collaborative care plans. • To support service users and colleagues to ensure that care plans are developed in partnership with the individual and their support network and that they reflect ‘recovery goals’. These should be strengths-based and oriented towards reinforcing a positive identity and developing valued social roles. • To be the allocated named worker for service users who have identified occupational performance needs or when occupational therapy is the main intervention. • To monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of occupational therapy interventions against clear aims, objectives and outcome measures in line with evidence-based practice and in conjunction with service users, carers/support network and other professionals. • To identify opportunities and needs for group work in the community and to plan, implement, facilitate and evaluate community groups which promote social inclusion for service users. • To apply a high level of understanding of the effects of mental illness and provide training and advice on lifestyle changes and adaptations to the service user’s social and physical environment. • To determine the impact of mental and physical conditions on service user’s functional ability and undertake assessment/make recommendations with regards to the provision of equipment/aids and adaptations. • To provide monitoring of medication, for all service users on caseload, in line with the CNWL OT Medication Management Guidelines. • To follow local protocol and obtain recommended equipment and/or liaise with local providers of equipment to ensure provision as appropriate. This advert closes on Thursday 20 Aug 2026. Permanent Full time

To work in partnership with Greenwich childrens social care by appropriately sharing health information and attending safeguarding meetings including child protection conferences, core groups and team around the child/family meetings where an identified health need requires a health intervention. Be proactive in the development, review and promotion of the Young Greenwich service. To maintain awareness and adherence to Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust policies and procedures and Young Greenwich standards. To support schools to achieve Healthy Schools accreditation and participation of the SHEU survey biannually. Support national and local health promotion campaigns whilst working with stakeholders and the wider Young Greenwich team. To work according to the NMC code, 6 Cs of nursing, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust Nursing Strategy and the ethos and aims of the Young Greenwich Partnership to ensure high quality, responsive patient focused care is delivered to all children and families. Management and Leadership responsibilities To plan own workload effectively to meet client needs, Young Greenwich activity targets and key touch points in accordance to the service offer. Participate in staff meetings / forums / specialist forums and working parties contributing to service development and maintain own professional knowledge. Support and advise schools / Families / GPs in relation to medicine management and the safe storage of emergency medication in schools highlighting expiry dates/ dosage requirements when required. To be an autonomous practitioner and follow the lone working policy to maintain safety. Research Contribute to service development ensuring that all care is evidence based, and implementing agreed changes. Contribute to Audit processes and the implementation of updated practices. To be proactive in ensuring where appropriate and able to do so a patient experience / service evaluation is captured. Communication and Record Keeping Establish and maintain good relationships with clients, carers and the wider partnership team. Communicate effectively with schools and parents in relation to the YG registration process, consent and YG referral pathway. To interpret sensitive information and communicate with a sympathetic and empathic approach to client centred care. Ensure effective verbal and written communication is maintained within the team at all times to ensure timely, effective and coordinated care for families. Maintain contemporaneous and accurate records daily on all active clients according to with record keeping standards, policy and NMC code using manual and electronic forms of recording including RiO diary outcomes for confirmation of contacts. Maintain IT systems such as RiO or CRM for the CYP registration, tracking, referrals and communicating across the partnership and to support reporting for key touch points. Ensure correct use of audiometers, scales and height metres, the calibration requirements of the equipment and report any deficiencies to PA or lead nurse. Responsible for the correct safe use of IT equipment such as laptop and reports defects to IT or Lead Nurse. To acknowledge that all work undertaken is of a highly confidential nature and therefore the need to observe and maintain this confidentiality is essential: general understanding of GDPR and process for reporting any data breaches in line with Trust policy. Complete and submit financial claims on a monthly basis within the deadline. To inform line manager of workload pressures that may adversely affect the level and quality of service provided. On Call/Unsocial Hours Core hours are Monday to Friday 9am-5pm. There may be occasional requirement to contribute to extended service hours of 8 am - 8 pm or weekend health promotion events.. eligibility_evidence.text: North West London Procurement Services (NWL PS), hosted by Central London Community Healthcare NHS Trust, provides strategic procurement and supply chain management services across NHS organisations within NW London. The Category Manager plays a key strategic role in leading the delivery of complex healthcare commissioning and procurement activity across the Integrated Care System (ICS). Working closely with Commissioners, Contracting, Finance and Operational colleagues, the postholder will lead elements of the commercial lifecycle, supporting the delivery of high-quality, value-driven healthcare services through strategic category management, procurement leadership and commercial planning. The postholder will contribute to the development and implementation of Category and Commercial Strategies, ensuring procurement activity is aligned to organisational priorities, and commissioning intentions. The role requires a strong understanding of the healthcare market, procurement legislation, commercial strategy and category management principles to provide expert advice and support to stakeholders. The Category Manager will have delegated responsibility for defined elements of the commercial lifecycle, including market intelligence, category planning, procurement strategy development, procurement governance and commercial work planning, supporting the delivery of innovative, compliant and value-for-money procurement solutions. You will play a key role in delivering strategic procurement and category management across a diverse portfolio of commissioned healthcare services. Your responsibilities will include: * Leading complex procurement projects from business case development through to contract award, ensuring compliance with Procurement Regulations. * Supporting the development and implementation of Category and Commercial Strategies aligned to commissioning priorities and organisational objectives. * Maintaining a strategic overview of the Community & Mental Health Services portfolio, identifying opportunities to improve value for money, standardise service provision and support service transformation. * Undertaking market analysis and market engagement activities to inform procurement strategies and commissioning decisions. * Managing procurement pipelines, through the Atamis e-sourcing system, ensuring accurate reporting and forward planning. * Providing specialist procurement advice and guidance to Commissioners, Contracting, Finance and Operational colleagues. * Developing strong collaborative relationships with stakeholders to support effective procurement planning and delivery. * Producing procurement reports, management information and commercial insights to support strategic decision-making. * Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives, procurement governance and the development of best practice procurement processes. eligibility_evidence.text: The Westminster Joint Homelessness Team (JHT) is a multi-agency service dedicated to supporting individuals who are homeless, rough sleeping, or at risk of homelessness within the City of Westminster. Working collaboratively with Westminster City Council, NHS services, housing providers, social care teams, substance misuse services, mental health services, and voluntary sector organisations, the team provides coordinated, person-centred interventions to address complex needs and improve long-term outcomes. The primary purpose of the team is to engage with vulnerable adults experiencing homelessness, assess their housing, health, and social care needs, and support them in accessing appropriate accommodation, healthcare, welfare benefits, and community resources. The service focuses on reducing rough sleeping, preventing homelessness, promoting recovery and independence, and improving overall wellbeing. Staff within the Joint Homelessness Team work closely with service users to develop tailored support plans, undertake comprehensive assessments, coordinate multi-disciplinary interventions, and advocate on behalf of individuals facing barriers to accessing services. The team operates within a trauma-informed and strengths-based framework, recognising the impact of homelessness, mental ill health, substance misuse, physical health conditions, and social exclusion. Key responsibilities include: Conducting comprehensive mental health and risk assessments, developing and reviewing recovery-focused care plans, managing a caseload of service users, administering and monitoring medication, and providing therapeutic interventions. The post holder works proactively to engage vulnerable individuals who may find it difficult to access mainstream services, often undertaking assessments and interventions in community settings such as hostels, temporary accommodation, day centres, and on outreach visits. The role involves close partnership working with housing services, Westminster City Council, social care, substance misuse services, primary care, inpatient services, and voluntary organisations to support access to housing, healthcare, and social support. The nurse is also responsible for safeguarding vulnerable adults, managing risk, contributing to Mental Health Act and Mental Capacity Act processes, and promoting recovery, independence, and social inclusion. As a senior practitioner, the Band 6 CPN provides leadership, supervision, and support to junior staff and students, contributes to service development and quality improvement initiatives, and ensures that all care is delivered in accordance with professional standards, Trust policies, and evidence-based practice. Working for Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust (CNWL) provides the opportunity to make a positive difference in the lives of people from diverse communities. It offers a supportive and collaborative environment where multidisciplinary working, professional development, and person-centred care are highly valued. Being part of a large NHS Trust enables staff to contribute to high-quality services, promote recovery and wellbeing, and work alongside partner agencies to improve outcomes for individuals with complex health and social care needs. Clinical Responsibilities • Undertake comprehensive mental health, psychosocial, and risk assessments for service users experiencing homelessness. • Assess, monitor, and manage risks relating to self-harm, suicide, exploitation, self-neglect, substance misuse, safeguarding, and risks to others. • Develop, implement, and regularly review recovery-focused, person-centred care plans. • Provide evidence-based mental health interventions and therapeutic support. • Monitor mental and physical health needs and facilitate access to primary and secondary healthcare services. • Administer and monitor prescribed medication, including depot injections where required. • Identify deterioration in mental state and coordinate timely interventions to prevent relapse and unnecessary hospital admissions. Care Coordination and Case Management • Manage a caseload of service users with severe and enduring mental illness and complex social needs. • Act as Care Coordinator in accordance with the Care Programme Approach (CPA) and Trust policies. • Support service users to engage with mental health services, housing providers, benefits systems, and community resources. • Promote service user involvement in care planning, goal setting, and decision-making. • Facilitate discharge planning and continuity of care following inpatient admissions. Homelessness and Housing Support • Work closely with Westminster City Council, outreach teams, housing providers, hostels, and supported accommodation services. • Contribute to housing assessments and support pathways into appropriate accommodation. • Assist service users in maintaining tenancy arrangements and reducing the risk of repeat homelessness. • Support individuals who have difficulty engaging with statutory services through assertive outreach and flexible engagement approaches. Multi-Agency Working • Work collaboratively with psychiatrists, GPs, social workers, occupational therapists, substance misuse services, probation services, safeguarding teams, and voluntary organisations. • Participate in multidisciplinary meetings and case conferences. • Provide specialist mental health advice and consultation to partner agencies working with homeless individuals. • Advocate for service users to ensure equitable access to healthcare, housing, and social care provisions. Safeguarding and Risk management • Identify and respond appropriately to adult and child safeguarding concerns. • Lead on risk management planning and ensure appropriate safeguarding procedures are followed. • Contribute to Mental Health Act assessments and Mental Capacity Act processes as required. • Maintain professional accountability for decision-making in complex and high-risk situations. Professional and Leadership Responsibilities • Provide supervision, support, and mentorship to junior staff, students, and support workers. • Contribute to service development, clinical audits, and quality improvement initiatives. • Maintain accurate, timely, and legally compliant clinical records. • Uphold NMC standards, Trust policies, and evidence-based practice. • Participate in continuing professional development and mandatory training. Assertive Outreach and Engagement • Conduct assessments and interventions in a range of community settings including streets, hostels, temporary accommodation, day centres, supported housing, and healthcare settings. • Use assertive outreach approaches to engage individuals who are reluctant or unable to access mainstream mental health services. • Develop therapeutic relationships with individuals who may have experienced trauma, exclusion, and repeated disengagement from services. • Work flexibly to improve engagement and continuity of care. • Maintain professional boundaries while building trust with vulnerable individuals.
